doc.title: Karl Berger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

title: Jimi Hendrix on the Dick Cavett Show
summary: Ingrid recalls Hendrix telling America to wake up on television and says creative expression keeps you awake.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: When we first came to the U.S. for the first time I saw Jimi Hendrix on television. Was it “The Dick Cavett Show?”

Cavett. And Dick Cavett said, “could you please say something to the world?” After the interview, to Jimi Hendrix. And he walked out on the microphone and said, “Americans wake up.” I don’t know whether he said “Americans” — no he didn’t.
And music helps not to put you asleep. Any creative expression helps to not put you to sleep.
